NEW YORK, Aug. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index® decreased by 0.8 points to 89.4 (1985=100) in August, down from 90.2 in July. The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—rose by 6.8 points to 121.2, following three months of consecutive decline. As the city heads back to school and approaches the major holiday season, we’ll continue to track the trends shaping NYC’s economy – and what they mean for New Yorkers.
